The game itself is pretty decent.
However:
- Premium currency, skins locked behind a paywall, vehicles locked behind paywall, pay to skip grind
- Battleye (no linux support included)
- FPS cap at 60
- ubisoft app constantly failing to synchronize some bs on a 1gbps connection
- No ability to play the game offline
- If you go afk for a few minutes (even if you're paused in a menu screen) the game will decide to kick you out into the main menu
- Lack of tutorials and explanations of core game systems, the tutorials that do exist don't actually explain anything and feel more like placeholders.
- Can't sort vehicles in the catalog, and the filters are pretty much useless.
- Always present mail envelope icon in the top left, which means: "nothing" if only they knew a better way to communicate you have no messages..
- AI blatantly cheating, driving impossible lines, gaining speed on sharp turns, being unaffected by obstacles.

Pros:
- your airplane can transform into a car and fall out of the sky
- they got rid of a lot of the story from the first Crew game and get you into the action arguably quicker
- gameplay is smoother than the original (fewer buggy connection issues)

Cons:
- there are still annoying cut scenes and a half baked story
- the world is not as memorable or interesting as the first game
- the terrain and weather was a lot more interesting in the original
- there's not much to do outside of the key spots spread out over the map
- they got rid of the whole cops chasing you concept when you cause destruction (although it is less annoying when you're trying to do something)
- all of the cars feel the same (driving off road with a Miata feels nearly the same as an offroad dune buggy)
- exploration is boring compared to similar games

Recommend playing the original instead. If you don't like story, try Forza Horizon or Burnout Paradise. All of them are much more enjoyable and interesting to just drive around in the world, in addition to being more fun when you do get into the action.

I used to play Asphalt 9 (with full assists) on my phone but my partner insisted I should play something more serious. So I got The Crew 2. I think it was the first time when I didn't pass the tutorial of the game on the first try. Flying is hard! This game definitely has a learning curve and takes some skill to master. But it still has something for more casual players as me. I like to play stories, do taxi, photo-op and skill missions. Off-road is one of my favourite disciplines (street racing has just too many turns). Boats at first looked really hard but now I enjoy them. Live Events are also fun, even if I can complete only a few races, at the end they give tons of followers which might be several levels for newer players. It seems that I already played a lot but there still is lots more to do.

Let me get right to the point. I would not recommend this game if you're looking for a good racing game. I would not recommend this game if you are all about graphics. I would not recommend this game if you like any sort of story line.

Update: ACE still isn't challenging, but I've learned to approach this game differently. If you really want to enjoy it after maxing out, try using lower tiered cars or putting more affixes towards loot find/quality. That helps keep the pack with you so that races don't get boring and you can still max out the car with gold parts to get the most from affixes.

They also added a massive amount of street races, and just about all of them are pretty well thought out, only one or two runs to get the track feel down. There are some exclusive cars due to season passes (motorpass), but none of them really top the leader boards so it's not a huge deal.

Originally I gave the game a negative review, but it's gone through a ton of updates. Some of the issues are still there like locked to 60hz refresh and the photo op/skill prompts during free roam still take up most of the screen for about 20 seconds every time you go through one.

What I like:
- Game has multiple disciplines (Street races, drift events, aerobatics, boat races, dirt bikes etc.)
- Has decent progression - you aren't handed decent cars early game like in Forza
- Huge map

What I dislike:
- AI rubberband
- Game has a 60 FPS cap - why?
- Voice acting is cringe
- Graphics are meh, yet the game runs pretty slow
- Handling is awful - cars have way too much body-roll and understeer as if they're driving on ice

Overall, this game is not worth the £50 that Ubisoft are asking for. However, I would recommend this game if it were around £30 instead.

I highly recommend this game even though it requires an online internet connection. This game has lots of cars including the all new Bugatti Divo, Aston Martin Vulcan, Bugatti Chiron, Lamborghini Egoista, F1 Cars, GP Grand Touring Circuit Cars, Awesome Rally Cars, Motocross, Super Bikes, Hover Crafts, Racing And Stunt Planes, Monster Trucks, Speed And Jet Boats, and Drift And Drag Racing Cars. Including a wide selection of races, trials, events, and awesome live summit events. Now let’s don’t forget the largest world map I’ve ever seen in one game an almost exact look a like of the great USA.

The Crew 2 is an awesome open-world driving game that I’ve really enjoyed. The ability to explore a vast map and drive a range of vehicles, especially the Lamborghini Aventador, makes for an exhilarating experience.

Although it’s been a while since I last played, the game was always a lot of fun and offered endless entertainment. If you enjoy open-world racing and variety in vehicles, it’s definitely worth checking out.

Rating: ★★★★☆

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (76%): players love the graphics and art and find the game fun to play.
The price is the most common complaint, and bugs and crashes leave some players unable to play.

details.text: Newer players who reviewed within their first 2 hours are mostly negative, at 24% positive, while players with more time are mostly positive.
The flagged wave of negative reviews in September 2024 matters less now that recent reviews are mostly positive.
